sections.title: Eleven herbs
text: A made-up form with a long group: eight herbs in the first group, three in the second, and two questions about each.

items.label: Basil
items.name: basil
items.definition: Tender leaves that bruise easily and want warmth and a lot of light.

items.label: Parsley
items.name: parsley
items.definition: Flat or curly, slow to sprout and then hard to stop.

items.label: Coriander
items.name: coriander
items.definition: Grown for its leaves first; it runs to seed as soon as it is warm.

items.label: Mint
items.name: mint
items.definition: Spreads by runners, so it is usually given a pot of its own.

items.label: Chives
items.name: chives
items.definition: Thin hollow leaves that grow back after every cut.

items.label: Dill
items.name: dill
items.definition: Feathery and tall, with a long root that dislikes being moved.

items.label: Tarragon
items.name: tarragon
items.definition: Narrow leaves with a taste of aniseed; it dies back in winter.

items.label: Chervil
items.name: chervil
items.definition: A delicate cousin of parsley that prefers shade.

items.label: Rosemary
items.name: rosemary
items.definition: An evergreen shrub with needles, happy to be dry.

items.label: Thyme
items.name: thyme
items.definition: Low and wiry, with tiny leaves and a liking for poor soil.

items.label: Sage
items.name: sage
items.definition: Soft grey leaves on a woody stem that needs cutting back each spring.

block.followUpsIntro: You gave up on {{count}} of these. One question about each.
